The AI economy is reorganizing the world's most important chip manufacturer in real time as HPC reaches 66% of $TSM revenue.

Even more impressive this record came with 2nm contributing just 3% of wafer revenue which means TSMC’s largest node transition has barely begun.

I'll be sharing my detailed $ASTS reaction on the Futurum Equities YouTube channel later today: 

piped.video/@FuturumEquities

$ASTS is down 15% after announcing a $1B convertible offering shortly after management said the company was fully funded for ~100 satellites.

While the financing terms are much better than the initial reaction suggests I think the timing communication and push of the 45-satellite target into early 2027 raise legitimate concerns around management credibility and execution.

The long-term opportunity is still intact which is why I added today but I think the market is reacting more to the delayed commercial ramp and inconsistent capital messaging than to the actual dilution as execution continues taking longer and costing more than management initially communicates.

Elon Musk says $SPCX AI satellites will use batteries to boost peak power from 150 kW to 230 kW.

The added power could reduce the number of satellites needed to reach the same compute capacity while lowering launch and manufacturing requirements.

$ASML has become one of the clearest ways to invest in the global AI chip buildout because it controls one of the most important bottlenecks in semiconductor manufacturing.

Its lithography systems act like ultra-precise printers that create the tiny circuit patterns used in advanced chips and ASML remains the only company producing EUV machines at scale.

$TSM cannot manufacture $NVDA Blackwell or Rubin GPUs without those systems which means nearly every dollar flowing into advanced AI compute ultimately passes through ASML’s equipment.

$BE is partnering with Industrial Development Funding and Oaktree on a $1.7B investment to deploy fuel cells for $NBIS AI cloud infrastructure.

The project will provide dedicated behind-the-meter power for AI compute with Morgan Stanley supporting the financing.

$MU signs a long-term supply agreement with $QCOM to provide memory and storage for AI-enabled vehicle platforms.

The deal supports infotainment ADAS and connectivity while giving Qualcomm greater supply and pricing visibility.

📺 HOW SUSTAINABLE IS THE SOFTWARE ROTATION? + DON'T BUY SEMIS UNTIL YOU SEE THIS

Try my Power Plays FREE for one week (July 20–24) – t3live.com/ppo-free

In this Short video, I explain why traders should pay close attention to the latest sector rotation before making their next move.

While semiconductors have dominated the market for months, institutional money is beginning to flow not only into Mag7 but also into software, creating a new set of opportunities for active traders.

*

One of the biggest clues came after $IBM earnings.

IBM sold off sharply, but instead of dragging the entire software sector lower, buyers stepped aggressively into names like $MSFT.

That relative strength was an early signal that institutions were treating IBM's weakness as company-specific rather than a reason to abandon software altogether.

#Microsoft followed through with a strong rally, while other software leaders like $PLTR, $NOW, and $CRM also started attracting buyers.

*

Successful traders don't stay married to yesterday's winners. 

Just a few months ago, memory $MU $SNDK and semiconductor $SOXX stocks were leading the market.

Now, leadership is shifting, and active traders need to adapt rather than force trades in weakening sectors.

Following the money (not the headlines) is often the key to staying on the right side of the trend.

*

This Short video also serves as a warning for semiconductor investors. $SOXL 

You need to respect technical support levels and follow disciplined risk management rules, such as exits below the 18- and 21-day moving averages.

Stocks that repeatedly test major support can become increasingly vulnerable, and if key levels fail, much larger declines can follow.

*

So, software $IGV is showing improving relative strength while parts of the semiconductor space remain under pressure.

Rather than automatically buying every dip in semis, you should watch where institutional money is rotating and let price action determine where the next leadership group will emerge.

*

📺 THE MEGA CAP ROTATION IS BACK – HERE'S HOW WE'RE TRADING IT

Try my Power Plays FREE for one week (July 20–24) – t3live.com/ppo-free

Looks like the market's leadership is rotating back toward mega-cap tech after semis $SOXX $SMH entered a multi-week correction.

While chip stocks $MU $SNDK have cooled off, names like $META, $AMZN, $AAPL, and also $NVDA are reclaiming relative strength, creating new swing trading opportunities for investors.

*

In this Short video, I walk through several recent trades, including $META explosive breakout that generated roughly 300% gains on call options for us, $AMZN long-awaited move above key resistance, and $AAPL continued respect for its 8-day moving average.

Reclaiming important technical levels can signal the start of fresh momentum, even after long periods of sideways price action.

*

I also cover the "rolling up options" strategy in detail.

Rather than simply holding, I repeatedly lock in profits, move into higher strike prices, and reduce capital at risk while staying positioned for additional upside.

Using $NVDA as an example, I explain how this disciplined process allowed me to participate in multiple legs higher without overexposing myself as the stock advanced.

Looking ahead, I believe #Nvidia sits at an important crossroads.

The key question is whether it will continue trading like the broader semiconductor group or fully rejoin the mega-cap leaders alongside #AMZN, $GOOGL, and the rest of the Magnificent Seven $MAGS.

If institutional money continues rotating into large-cap technology, those stocks could remain the market's primary source of leadership in the weeks ahead.

*

Whether you're an options trader or a swing trader, this video offers practical lessons on identifying leadership rotation, managing winning positions, and maximizing gains as trends unfold without increasing risk.
